newsitem.title: USA: Alumax downplays second officer resignation.
newsitem.headline: Alumax downplays second officer resignation.

text.p: The resignation of Alumax Inc's chief financial officer Lawrence Frost is the second resignation of a top company executive in five months but the company is downplaying any connection between the two.
"It would be a mistake to draw a connection between the two," a company spokesman told Reuters.

The resignation of Frost, 54, comes on the heels of the departure of George Stoe, an executive vice president and director who resigned in March after 27 years of service amid disagreements with Allen Born, Alumax's chief executive officer.

"George Stoe had disagreements with management over the direction of the company. Frost has been with the company for 25 years and he was just looking for new challenges," the company spokesman added.
Analysts, on the other hand, were surprised by Frost's resignation.
"It's very odd to see the departure of two top executives in such a short period of time," said one analyst. "It seems like there's some dissatisfaction with the pace of the restructuring."
The Alumax spokesman denied this was the case.
In the last two years, Alumax began shifting its downstream product mix toward more value-added products.
"It suprised me," said Clarence Morrision, an analyst with Prudential Securities. "54 years old seems pretty young to be tired of what you do."
But he stopped short of drawing a correlation between Stoe and Frost's departures. "There were very obvious divisions between Stoe and Born. But Born and Larry (Frost) always seemed to get along."
He warned of a "financial vacuum" at the upper rungs of management, which "has always been Alumax's strong suit. Frost left them in pretty good shape, but they're going to need a good successor."
The spokesman said no successor has been named. He said he didn't know where Frost would go next.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
